title: Effects of subjective and objective autoregulation methods for intensity and volume on enhancing maximal strength during resistance-training interventions: a systematic review
population: 14 studies, 30 training groups and 356 healthy participants.
key_findings: Every autoregulated protocol in the included studies increased 1RM, with small to large effect sizes.
Both subjective methods (RIR-based RPE, flexible daily undulating periodization) and objective methods (velocity targets, velocity loss) appear effective for maximal strength.
The authors speculate that autoregulation helps because it accounts for daily fluctuations in fitness, fatigue and readiness.
methods: Systematic review with per-study effect sizes and percentage differences; no pooled meta-analysis.
limitations: Strength outcomes only; no pooled estimate; the proposed mechanism is speculative by the authors' own wording.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
